doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Mountain climbing, trail running and music
summary: Rowe says trail running and hiking give perspective that helps solve musical and personal problems.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I see that, I forget where it was mentioned that you’re a — here it says right here — accomplished outdoors woman, mountain climber and trail hiker.
So I’m picturing you, can you remove music — something you’re working on — when you go out and hike? Or is it always like intruding on your thoughts.

Well I mean my two passions are mountain climbing and actually trail running. And so when I’m running on the trails there may be a musical backdrop but when you’re trail running you have to be super focused on where you’re putting your feet and so yeah, not so much — when I’m hiking definitely, yeah. I mean there’s always something going on. And even with the trail running I mean I know I’m sort of problem solving, you know musical things when I’m running. But yeah, the focus with the trail running again, you know, as I’ve got some cuts and scrapes all over my body from falls I’ve taken. But yeah, not the music is sort of always there just in differing degrees. But what I find from both of those experiences is that when I’m finished there’s a sense of perspective that both helps solve musical dilemmas and personal dilemmas, even if I haven’t necessarily been thinking about those specific things while I’m out there, but just for me, and I really preach this to my students just being out in nature, period. It’s so incredibly important. And moving through nature fast, you know when you’re running or slower when you’re hiking, just kind of centers me and I find it really centers our students as well. We have a

lot of meditation classes as part of our program as well. And some of it is outdoor walking meditations. I don’t teach those but yeah. So there’s definite problem solving that goes on, sometimes unconsciously.
